title: Micron Stock Is STILL Dirt Cheap After This Massive Beat!!
creator: Jose Najarro Stocks
summary: In 'Micron Stock Is STILL Dirt Cheap After This Massive Beat!!' (published 1 Oct 2026, covering Micron's Sep 30 post-close print), Jose Najarro — who does not own the stock — argues the triple beat (revenue, EPS, and next-quarter guidance all well above consensus) leaves Micron cheap, with the flat after-hours reaction reflecting already-high hopes. His bull case: pricing is doing the heavy lifting (DRAM revenue +27% YoY, NAND +42%, on only mid-single-digit bit growth), and Micron expects a tight market through 2027-28 even with mid-20s industry bit-shipment growth; 35% of revenue through 2030 is covered by multi-year take-or-pay contracts, with $150B of remaining performance obligations (at minimum contract prices, so the real figure could be much higher) and $32B in customer cash deposits. HBM repricing begins at the start of calendar 2027, Q1 is the gross-margin floor, and buybacks unlock after December 9 (the CHIPS Act incentive 2-year anniversary) — he would not be surprised by a $50B repurchase authorization. Watch items: DRAM sequential price growth is decelerating (from ~60% to the high teens), consumer PC/phone units face double-digit declines in 2026, and capex is stepping up past $50B in 2027 (funded by contracted demand, he stresses). Caveat: auto-captions heavily garble the reported figures (e.g. '$54.2 billion in revenue', '$33 in one quarter' EPS, '$60 to 63 billion' guide) — treat all numbers here as approximate. Call: MU — BUY ('still dirt cheap'), with a rerating as the prize and supply-tight AI demand as the engine. Also bullish on the wider semiconductor/neocloud space as a memory bottleneck 'extends the cycle'.
